technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Boot for application setup, dependency management, and configuration.
Leverage Spring Kafka library for Kafka integration to handle producer and consumer implementations efficiently.
For Sqoop integration, use Java's ProcessBuilder to execute Sqoop commands and capture logs, as Sqoop primarily operates via command-line interface.
Implement Kafka concurrency using Spring Kafka's producer and consumer pool configurations with configurable thread counts.
Support Kafka compression by setting producer/consumer properties (e.g., snappy, lz4) via Spring configuration.
ACK options will utilize Kafka's transactional support or manual acknowledgment modes for reliable message delivery.
Implement request-reply patterns using correlation IDs and temporary topics for async communication between requestors and repliers.
Enable batching through Kafka producer settings like batch.size and linger.ms, configurable via Spring properties.
Sqoop job stopping implemented by managing process lifecycle, sending interrupt signals, or invoking Sqoop's job control features.
Capture Sqoop logs by redirecting stdout/stderr streams to SLF4J or application logging frameworks for monitoring.
Incremental data load in Sqoop configured via command-line parameters (--incremental, --check-column, --last-value) exposed through application interfaces.
Ensure all configurations support global defaults with per-deployment overrides using Spring profiles or property files.
assumptions: The project is within an existing Spring-based application, so no full framework setup is required from scratch.
Development environment includes Java 17+, Spring Boot, Kafka (e.g., Apache Kafka), and Sqoop installed or accessible via dependencies.
Sqoop is available and can be invoked via command line; no need for Sqoop Java API integration.
Estimates include only development effort (coding, unit testing, documentation) and exclude deployment, production setup, or extensive manual testing.
All user stories are independent and can be implemented sequentially without significant dependencies.
A single developer with experience in Java, Spring, and Kafka is performing the work, ensuring efficient implementation.
Acceptance tests and integration tests are part of the scope and will use standard frameworks like JUnit and Spring Test.
Logging mechanisms for Sqoop are compatible with existing application logs, assuming SLF4J or similar is used.

activities.activity_description: Set up the development environment by configuring Spring Boot project, adding necessary dependencies (Spring Kafka, Sqoop-related libraries if any), and establishing build scripts.
Analyze user stories, design system architecture, define interfaces and classes for Kafka and Sqoop features, and create a detailed implementation plan.

Implement concurrency support for Kafka producers and consumers with configurable thread pools, and add compression options (e.g., snappy, lz4) via Spring configuration properties with global defaults and per-deployment overrides.
Implement message acknowledgment options for Kafka, including transactional producers and consumer acknowledgments, to guarantee successful message delivery.
Develop bindRequestor and bindReplier components for async request-reply communication using Kafka, involving correlation IDs and temporary topics for replies.
Enable batching support for Kafka data ingestion by configuring producer batch settings (e.g., batch.size, linger.ms) and ensuring integration with Spring Kafka templates.
Implement functionality to stop existing Sqoop jobs by managing process lifecycle, capturing job IDs, and using Sqoop's job control features or interrupt signals.
Capture Sqoop logs by redirecting command-line output streams to application logging mechanisms (e.g., SLF4J) and provide access via API or UI for troubleshooting.
Implement incremental data load for Sqoop by exposing configuration options for date or ID-based increments and integrating with Sqoop command-line parameters.
Write unit tests for all implemented Kafka and Sqoop features to ensure code correctness and coverage, using JUnit and mocking frameworks.
Implement acceptance tests for Kafka as a message bus to validate functionality, and integrate them into CI builds using frameworks like Cucumber or Spring Test.
Perform end-to-end integration tests for Kafka and Sqoop features to ensure they work together seamlessly in a realistic environment.
Document the implementation details, create API references, and conduct code reviews to maintain code quality and knowledge sharing.
